Joice, twenty lessons. What are you going to do next?
I am going to continue. I am going to speak in every meeting.
Every meeting? That is a big decision.
Not a big one. One sentence is enough. But I am going to say it every time.
And what are you going to do about November?
I am going to prepare three minutes, and I am not going to read them.
Are you going to be nervous?
Yes, I am. And I am going to do it anyway.
That is the whole method, in one sentence. Anything else?
One more thing: I am not going to use the translator in the meetings.
I am going to be nervous, and I am going to do it anyway.
On the fifth of November I am presenting in Belém.

Dear group, thank you for the first part of the year. Here is what we are going to do next. We are going to continue the work with public schools, and we are going to prepare a new report together. The first version is going to be ready in October. We are not going to work with the big schools this semester: we decided to give all our time to the small ones. In November we are going to Belém, and five people from this group are presenting there. Thank you, and see you soon.

Hi, Joice. This is a message only for you. Twenty lessons ago you recorded one minute about your work, and you could not finish it. Today you record two minutes and you do not stop. Nothing changed in your intelligence, and nothing changed in your accent. What changed is that you tried, twice a week, for twenty lessons. In November you are going to speak in Belém. You are going to be nervous, and you are going to do it anyway. That is the whole method.

Joice listens to her first recording from lesson one. She listens to her recording from lesson nineteen. She writes three things that are different. She decides what she is going to do in the next block. She sends her plan to the teacher.
